clue.text: Deny trading is down

indicators.note: trading means exchanging, so the letters of the next two words swap places among themselves

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A broker denies that the market has fallen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trading' looks like stock-market talk but signals rearranging IS DOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown something is to refuse to acknowledge it, a synonym for deny.

clue.text: Idiot in the face of modern media technology

indicators.note: in means placed inside another word

parts.note: a dial is the face of a clock or watch
git is British slang for an idiot

explanation.surface: A fool confronts the latest gadgets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the face' reads as confronting something, but a clock's face is what is meant; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Digital describes computer-based electronic technology, the basis of modern media.

clue.text: The girl with record of livestock

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a girl
EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A farm girl keeps records of her animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheep are farm animals, a common type of livestock.

clue.text: Raindrop

parts.note: read as rain drop, a fall of water rather than a single droplet

explanation.definitionFit: A cascade is water dropping from a height, which the split word describes.

clue.text: McCitizen?

parts.note: the Mc prefix evokes a fast-food chain's sandwich, while the word citizen points to a town dweller whose title sounds just like that sandwich

explanation.surface: A coined word for a fast-food chain's customer.
explanation.definitionFit: A burgher is a citizen of a town, and the word sounds like the beef patty sold by the Mc chain.

clue.text: Grows fat with 19 25s to face a storm

definitions.meaning: to grow fat or thrive at another's expense
secures ship openings against bad weather, completed by the linked lights

explanation.definitionFit: To batten is to thrive or fatten; sailors also fasten covers with wooden strips before a gale.

clue.text: Took horse to ring at a show

parts.note: rode means travelled on horseback
O is round like a ring

explanation.surface: A rider took a horse into the arena at an exhibition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo is a show of cowboy skills such as riding broncos.

clue.text: How not to respond to a flasher?

definitions.text: How not to respond to a flasher?

parts.words: How not to respond to a flasher?
parts.note: a flasher reveals himself; the advice would be not to expose oneself back, while the phrase really means to confront someone

explanation.surface: Advice on dealing with an indecent exposer.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle a dispute by open confrontation is the idiom's sense.

clue.text: Animal makes nest in rubbish

indicators.note: in means placed inside another word

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish
a den is an animal's lair or nest

explanation.surface: A creature builds its home in a heap of refuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' is only a link joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodent is a gnawing mammal such as a rat or mouse.

clue.text: Crush for a fictional lawyer lacking love

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so a letter is removed

parts.note: Rumpole of the Bailey is a fictional barrister in British TV and books
love is zero in tennis, hence O

explanation.surface: A fictional barrister has a crush with no love returned.
explanation.definitionFit: To rumple is to crumple or crease, a sense of crush.

clue.text: Wild rage at jibe from a relative

indicators.note: wild suggests something out of control, so the letters of rage run loose

parts.note: a jibe is a taunt

explanation.surface: Someone is furious at a cutting remark from a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges RAGE into GREA; 'at' and 'from a' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A great-aunt is a parent's aunt, a kind of family relative.

clue.text: Daughter keen on a boy

parts.note: keen means eager or avid

explanation.surface: A daughter has her eye on a young man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' simply joins the pieces in a down-the-page sense here.
explanation.definitionFit: David is a common male name, so an example of a boy.

clue.text: Animal said to slim towards the tail

indicators.note: said tells us the word is heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: to taper is to grow slimmer towards one end

explanation.surface: A creature is described as narrowing towards its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The tapir is a hoofed mammal of tropical America and Asia with a short trunk.

clue.text: Greek vestment to help out with tear-jerker

indicators.note: out means not in proper order, so the letters of help are jumbled

parts.note: an onion makes the eyes water when cut

explanation.surface: Someone is offered help with a sad film while dressing for church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges HELP into PHEL; 'tear-jerker' sounds like a weepy film but is the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: The phelonion is the outer liturgical vestment of an Orthodox priest, akin to a chasuble.

clue.text: Deceive about fermented drink which is an innocuous one

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: to deceive is to lie
mead is a drink fermented from honey

explanation.surface: Someone is lying about a strong honey drink to pass it off as harmless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' in the definition refers back to the drink, and 'which is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Limeade is a soft lime-flavoured drink, harmless compared with an alcoholic brew.

clue.text: Canteen provides green cooking for the ambassador

parts.note: a mess is a military canteen

indicators.note: cooking suggests something being worked up or mixed, so green is rearranged

explanation.surface: The embassy canteen prepares vegetables for the envoy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' turns GREEN into ENGER; 'provides' and 'for the' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambassador carries messages between governments, a kind of envoy.

clue.text: Laterally English get in old port

indicators.note: get in tells us one piece enters inside the other

parts.note: Sidon was an ancient Phoenician port

explanation.surface: An Englishman sneaks sideways into an ancient harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Side-on means viewed or approached from the side, which is what laterally conveys.

clue.text: Spooner's municipal sewer prescribed for a lazy student

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the starting sounds of words

parts.note: municipal means belonging to the town
a sewer is a drain

explanation.surface: A Spoonerism about town plumbing turns into advice for a slacker.
explanation.walkthrough: A student sent down from university for idleness would leave by a train heading away from London.
explanation.definitionFit: A down train leaves the capital, the journey for a student sent down from college.

clue.text: One enjoys stable employment in travel accommodation

definitions.text: One enjoys stable employment in travel accommodation

parts.words: One enjoys stable employment in travel accommodation
parts.note: stable employment reads as a secure job but literally means work in the stables, here those of a coaching inn

explanation.surface: Someone has a secure job in the hotel trade.
explanation.definitionFit: An ostler was the man who looked after travellers' horses at an inn.

clue.text: Uniform such as is brought into rural fashion

indicators.note: is brought into means put inside another set of letters
to fashion is to shape anew, so rural is rearranged

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation for for example

explanation.surface: Countrywear is introduced as uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' gives RULAR, a rearrangement of the countryside word, which is then opened after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Regular can mean even and consistent throughout, a sense of uniform.

clue.text: Cheers!

parts.note: a drinking toast, said as the glass is raised and emptied

explanation.definitionFit: This phrase is a jocular toast urging a drink to be swallowed, like saying cheers.

clue.text: Being fond of your pet involves money

indicators.note: involves means wraps around, so one word holds the other

parts.note: a dog is a common pet
tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: Lavishing cash on one's pet animal.
explanation.walkthrough: Tin is old British slang for cash; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Doting means showing excessive fondness, as a besotted owner does.

clue.text: Makes safe motions to bring down government by decapitating them

indicators.note: decapitating removes the head, the first letter of the word

parts.note: censures are parliamentary motions of no confidence

explanation.surface: Parliament plots to bring down a government by beheading its members.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure is to make certain or secure, hence to make safe.

clue.text: Direction in scriptural work is of no consequence

indicators.note: in means placed inside another word

parts.note: Tobit is a book of the Apocrypha
W is west, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A minor scriptural text is said to be unimportant.
explanation.walkthrough: W goes inside TOBIT, a book found in the Apocrypha; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Two-bit means cheap or trivial, of little consequence.

clue.text: Hardly Falstaff late on a Wednesday evening, say

indicators.note: say tells us the phrase is spoken, so its sound counts rather than its spelling

parts.note: Falstaff is Shakespeare's fat, hearty knight, the very opposite of a feeble one

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's fat knight carousing late midweek.
explanation.walkthrough: Falstaff, the corpulent knight of Henry IV, is hardly a weak knight; 'late on a' is a link phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Wednesday evening is an example of an evening falling on a working day.

clue.text: Brown turns up at church of course

indicators.note: in a down clue turns up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: tan is a shade of brown

explanation.surface: Mr Brown appears at church, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' looks like a surname; 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Natch is informal shorthand for naturally, meaning of course.

clue.text: Calls to dogs to stop — shoot's over

indicators.note: over suggests being knocked over, so the letters of shoot tumble into a new order

parts.note: shoot's reads as shoot is, the 's being a link

explanation.surface: Hunters call off the dogs because the shooting has finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Toho is a hunter's cry ordering pointing dogs to halt, so these are such cries.

clue.text: see 19 across
Major theological work for a fundamentalist?

parts.note: major means large or big
OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A large religious text for a hardline believer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigot holds narrow views intolerantly, as a fundamentalist may be thought to.

clue.text: Ancestral development of royal house

indicators.note: development means change or growth, so the letters of ancestral are reworked

explanation.surface: How a noble family grew from its ancestors.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancaster was the English royal house of Henry IV, V and VI.

clue.text: Penalty pronounced on arsonist?

indicators.note: pronounced tells us a word is heard spoken aloud

parts.note: torture is a cruel penalty

explanation.surface: A sentence is passed on a fire-raiser.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who torches buildings could whimsically be called this, hence the question mark for an arsonist.

clue.text: Moves slowly in unfinished game

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the game is left off

parts.note: chess is a board game

explanation.surface: Players creep along in a match not yet over.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch is to move slowly and carefully, a little at a time.
